gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Plakkaat draws heavy letters like bent straws, terminals curling round until they almost meet the stem. Noto Sans Tagalog opens up in reply, its middle zone dominant and its curve gaps generous.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: Plakkaat builds heavy letters from bent-straw lines, with terminals that curl round to the brink of the stem and close up. Noto Sans Tai Viet adds open curves and short ascenders beneath it.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-takri: Plakkaat's round bowls keep one thickness all the way round, heavy lines bent like straws. Noto Sans Takri brings its best feature, a sans-serif lowercase with generously unclosed curves and a high waist.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement has round forms like open parentheses. Over a full page its stocky middle band gives lines a dense, steady feel, while heavy Plakkaat headings stay closed and tight above.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Heavy, rope-thick curves, with Plakkaat bending every line like a straw and keeping capitals close to lowercase height. Noto Sans Tangsa lets wide, inviting round letters and short ascenders ease the weight above.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Bold Plakkaat closes its curves while Noto Sans Telugu opens them. Down a full column, Noto Sans Telugu reads in a brisk, businesslike way, its high midline and outward-opening counters keeping the text light.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Chunky, closed-in lettering from Plakkaat, drawn like bent straws. Noto Sans Thai Looped makes the strongest case, since its sans-serif lowercase looks bold from sheer body size and its curve terminals stay spacious.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho hits hard with a hulking lowercase, like thick chalk pressed down, and an e with a wide gap. But Plakkaat's talent is constant weight along every curve, in lines bent like straws.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Approachable is the body here: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square has a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Plakkaat, closed and heavy, would lose its punch if shrunk small.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-orienta: Modern Orienta breathes through counters like a hollow reed cut open, under Plakkaat's heavy, closed straw-bent lines. Orienta reads smoothly down a full column, its small gap between capital and lowercase height keeping lines level.
